questions.question: Flagella are the hair-like structures which act as organelles of locomotion in which of the following organisms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Bacteria.**__

__
 
• Flagella have a filamentous structure that helps in the locomotion of **Archea, Bacteria, and Eukaryotes**.
 
• Flagellum means ‘**whip**’ and this whip-like structure enables a cell to propel in liquid.
 
• Some flagella act as sensory organs in few organisms that sense changes in pH and temperature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

Flagella are composed of **flagellin** protein which makes its helical structure. **Its structure is divided into three parts **–

 
• **Basal Body**: attached to the cell membrane and cytoplasmic membrane and consists of rings surrounded by MotB protein.
 
• **Hook**: connects motor protein in the base to the filament.
 
• **Filament**: thin hair-like structure arising from the Hook.

**Functions of Flagella:**

 
• Helps in locomotion
 
• Act as sensory organs (sense pH and temperature)
 
• Increase reproduction rates in few eukaryotes
 
• Used as a Secretary organelle in **Chlamydomonas**

**Types of Flagella:**

 
• **Monotrichous**: Single flagellum at one pole
 
• **Amphitrichous:** Single flagellum at each pole
 
• **Lophotrichous**: 2 or more flagellum at one or both poles

 4. **Peritrichous**: Flagellum all over the surface

**Structure of Flagella**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/20eef1f2426fcedcaf46f4cfff86dcf120c08e9c2fe73e25a83432f07096cd54.png]

questions.question: Tiny pores present on the surface of leaves are known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**stomata**__.

__
 
• **Tiny pores present on the surface of leaves are known as stomata**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Stomata:**

 
 
• Stomata are small pores present in the epidermis of leaves, stems and other plant parts.
 
• The stomata are surrounded by two guard cells.
 
• This allows gases such as carbon dioxide, water vapor and oxygen to diffuse into and out of the plant's internal tissues.
 
• It occurs mostly in vascular plants.
 
• The inner wall of the guard cell is thicker than the outer wall.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nucleus**

 
 
• It was discovered by **Robert Brown**.
 
• The nucleus is **rich in protein** and **RNA**.
 
• **Chromatin **is the controlling **center of a cell.**
 
 
 
• **Mitochondria:**
 
 
• It is a **semi-autonomous organelle** and called the **powerhouse **of the cell because in it stepwise oxidation of fuel occurs which results in a release of chemical energy.
 
• This **energy is stored in the form of ATP.**
 
 
 
• The **cytoplasm **is the fluid found **outside the nuclear membrane.**

questions.question: Which of the following symmetries is exhibited by arthropods?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** **__**Bilateral.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **If the body can be divided into identical left and right halves in only one plane, this type of body plan is called bilateral symmetry.**
 
• **Example - annelids, arthropods, etc.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d9bd25cd09f2de39b07b2584c69cba1751d42997efb5fcf3955f42388b083faa.png] 

Fig: Bilateral Symmetry

 
• Animals can be categorized into** three types on the basis of their symmetry - Asymmetrical, Radial symmetry & Bilateral symmetry.**
 
• Radial symmetry
 
 
• **When any plane passing through the central axis of the body divides the organism into two identical halves, it is called radial symmetry.**
 
• Radial symmetry is exhibited by Coelenterates, ctenophores, and echinoderms.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/837e5518146c767d9e994377211d886ee590f83ffe302dbe85d496a8261be2f9.png] 

Fig: Radial Symmetry

 
• **Asymmetrical**

 
 
• If any plane that passes through the centre does not divide them into equal halves, this type of body plan is called asymmetrical.** Example - Porifera (Sponges).​**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Arthropods are invertebrate animals having an exoskeleton, a segmented body, and paired jointed appendages.** 
 
• Arthropods form the **phylum Arthropoda.** 
 
• They are** distinguished by their jointed limbs and cuticle made of chitin, **often mineralized with calcium carbonate.
 
• The** largest phylum in the animal kingdom**, includes **lobsters, crabs, spiders, mites, insects, centipedes, and millipedes**.
 
• About** 84 percent of all known species of animals are members of this phylum.**

questions.question: Which of the following has seeds with two cotyledons?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rose.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Roses are **dicotyledon or dicots** as they have two cotyledons, the first seed leaf, which is present in the embryo.
 
• Other characteristics are reticulate venation in leaves, monocots generally have parallel venation. 
 
• The cotyledons act as a food store in plant seeds.
 
• Cotyledons are often fleshy and full of reserve food materials.
 
• Based on the number of cotyledons vascular plants can be classified as Monocot and Dicot.
 
• Cot word represents the cotyledons, which means an embryonic leaf

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Two different types of cotyledon are Monocotyledons and Dicotyledons.
 
• Monocot-
 
 
• Monocotyledons are the angiosperms or the flowering plants in which the seeds typically contain only one embryonic leaf or Cotyledon.
 
• Example- Ginger, onions, wheat, and grass.
 
 
 
• Dicot- 
 
 
• Dicotyledons are the angiosperms or the flowering plants in which the seeds contain two embryonic leaves or cotyledons.
 
• Example- All legumes including beans, lentils, pea, rose and peanuts

questions.question: Proboscis gland for excretion is present in the phylum:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hemichordata**__.

__
 
• **The probosci's gland for excretion is present in the Hemichordata phylum**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hemichordata**:

 
 
• It is a phylum of **marine invertebrates.**
 
• They are found in a wide range of** depths and habitats in the oceans.**
 
• The body is mainly divided into three parts:** proboscis (protostome), collar (mesosome) and trunk (metasome).**
 
• They show all the characteristics of **Deuterostomia **and at least one unique structure i.e. the stomochord which is a cartilaginous element that projects into the protocoel and supports the heart and kidney complex. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phylum Mollusca:**

 
 
• The body is divided into the head and muscular foot.
 
• The mantle is always present in it.
 
• The alimentary canal is well developed.
 
• Respiration takes place through gills or ctenidia.
 
• Blood is colourless.
 
• Excretion takes place through the kidneys.
 
• Example: Pila, Octopus.
 
 
 
• **Phylum Arthropoda**
 
 
• The body is divided into three parts– Head, Thorax and Abdomen.
 
• The body is covered with a thick chitinous exoskeleton.
 
• Jointed leg.
 
• The circulatory system is of open type.
 
• Its body cavities are called haemocoels.
 
• The trachea, book lungs, body surface are respiratory parts.
 
• These are mainly unisexual and fertilization takes place inside the body.
 
• Example: Cockroach and Prawn.
 
 
 
• **Phylum Porifera:**
 
 
• All animals of this group are found in water and bear pores in the body.
 
• These are multicellular animals but cells do not make regular tissues.
 
• Numerous pores are known as Ostia found on the body wall.
 
• Skeleton is made up of minute calcareos or silicon spicules.
 
• Examples: Sycon, Sponge, etc.

questions.question: Ciliate, or Ciliophoran are the member of which of the following phylums?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Protozoa.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ciliate, or ciliophoran, any member of the protozoan phylum Ciliophora,** is generally **considered the most evolved and complex of protozoans.**
 
• **Ciliophora (phylum Protozoa)is a subphylum of protozoa** in which cilia are present during at least one stage of the life cycle.
 
• **Two different types of nucleus (macronucleus and micronucleus) are normally present.**
 
• **Cells reproduce by binary fission.**
 
• Some examples of the phylum Ciliophora include:
 
 
• Spirostomum ambiguum
 
• Strombidium lagenula
 
• Paramecium caudatum
 
• Paramecium aurelia
 
• Spirostomum minus etc.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** ​Sipuncula**

 
 
• ​The Sipuncula or Sipunculida is a class containing about 162 species of unsegmented marine annelid worms.
 
• **Scientific name:** Sipuncula.**​​**
 
• **Phylum: **Annelida.
 
• **Kingdom: **Animalia.
 
 
 
• **Rotifers**
 
 
• ​The rotifers, commonly called wheel animals or wheel animalcules, make up a phylum of microscopic and near-microscopic pseudocoelomate animals. 
 
• **Scientific name:** Rotifera.
 
• **Phylum:** Rotifera.
 
• **Kingdom: **Animalia.
 
 
 
• **Echinoderm**
 
 
• ​An echinoderm is any member of the** phylum Echinodermata.**
 
• The adults are recognisable by their** radial symmetry, **and include** starfish, brittle stars, sea urchins, sand dollars, and sea cucumbers, **as well as the **sea lilies or "stone lilies".**
 
• **Kingdom:** Animalia.
 
• **Subkingdom: **Eumetazoa.
 
 
 
• **Protozoa**
 
 
• ​Protozoa is an informal term for a group of **single-celled eukaryotes**, either** free-living or parasitic,** that** feed on organic matter such as other microorganisms or organic tissues and debris.**

questions.question: Which of the following animals breathes through its skin?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Frog**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The frog breathes through its skin.**

 
• Respiration is the process of exchanging gases in all life forms between an organism and its environment, which can occur in different ways, either independently or in tandem.
 
• The gills of a newly hatched Tadpole are external. When water passes over these gills, they take in oxygen.
 
• The gills are absorbed by the body as the tadpole matures, and become an internal part of the anatomy of the tadpole.
 
• Frogs can live both on land and in freshwater and belong to the class Amphibia of phylum Chordata.
 
• Frogs respire on land and in the water by two different methods. In water, skin acts as a respiratory organ(i.e cutaneous respiration) by diffusion.

 [IMAGE: https://www.brown.edu/Departments/Engineering/Courses/En123/MuscleExp/ImgSource/frog_gas_exchange.gif] ​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Respiration is of 2 types:

 
 

 
 
Aerobic Respiration

 
 
 
Anaerobic Respiration

 
 
 

 
 
It takes place in the presence of oxygen.

 
 
 
It takes place in the absence of oxygen.

 
 
 

 
 
A complete breakdown of food occurs.

 
 
 
A partial breakdown of food occurs.

 
 
 

 
 
The end products are carbon dioxide and water.

 
 
 
The end products may be ethanol and carbon dioxide as found in yeast or lactic acid as seen in animal muscles.

 
 
 

 
 
It releases 38 ATP per glucose molecule.

 
 
 
It releases only 2 ATP per glucose molecule.

questions.question: All living organisms are classified into _______ kingdoms under the system proposed by Whittaker (1969),
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Five.__

__
 
• All living organisms are classified into **five **kingdoms under the system proposed by **Robert Whittaker** in1969.
 
• They are **Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• Monera__ is a kingdom that contains unicellular organisms with a prokaryotic cell organization having no nuclear membrane such as bacteria.

 __
 
• They contain 70S ribosomes and DNA is naked.
 
• They reproduce asexually by binary fission or budding.
 
• They do not possess any membrane-bound organelles.
 
• They are found mostly in a moist environment like hot springs, snow, deep oceans, or as parasites in other organisms.
 
 
 
• Animalia__ kingdom includes all animals.
 __
 
• Animals are multicellular, eukaryotic organisms.
 
• Animals are heterotrophic, obtaining their energy by consuming energy-releasing food substances.
 
• Animals typically reproduce sexually.
 
• Animals are made up of cells that do not have cell walls.
 
 
 
• Protista__ is a kingdom of simple eukaryotic organisms, usually composed of a single cell or a colony of similar cells.
 __
 
• Protists live in water, in moist terrestrial habitats, and as parasites and other symbionts in the bodies of multicellular eukaryotes.
 
 
 
• **Fungi__ are eukaryotic organisms that include microorganisms such as **yeasts, moulds and mushrooms.
 __
 
• They can be either **single-celled or multicellular organisms**.
 
• Fungi contain a cell wall and are omnipresent.
 
 
 
• **Plantae**__ kingdom is filled with all eukaryotes which have chloroplast.
 
 
• Most of them are **autotrophic in nature, but some are heterotrophic as well.**
 
• The Cell wall **mainly comprises cellulose.**
 
• They have photosynthesis pigment so that they can prepare food their own food.
 
• Organisms in this group **reproduce sexually or asexually.**

questions.question: Amoeba pushes out one or more finger-like projections called ______ or false feet for movement and capture of food.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**pseudopodia.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An amoeba often known as an amoeboid is a microscopic unicellular animal found in pond water. 
 
• It has a **cell membrane, a rounded, dense nucleus**, and many small **bubble-like vacuoles** in its cytoplasm.
 
• It constantly changes its shape and position. 
 
• It pushes out one, or more finger-like projections, called pseudopodia or false feet for movement and capture of food.
 
• It feeds on some microscopic organisms. 
 
• When it senses food, it pushes out one or more finger-like projections **pseudopodia** around the food particle and engulfs it.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Food vacuoles** - These helps digests the food in Amoeba.
 
• **Contractile vacuoles** - Wastes and excess water are transported outside the cell by it.
 
• **Endoplasm** - It refers to the inner and dense part of the cytoplasm of the cell.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/237355e7b33aa6521f046509ab806135ff6ca42318d242cf180c3f7f1c050573.png]

questions.question: What is the network of air tubes for gas exchange in insects?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tracheae**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the respiratory system of insects **oxygen and carbon dioxide gases ****are exchanged through a network of tubes called tracheae**.
 
• Air enters and exits the respiratory systems of insects through a series of external openings called **spiracles.**
 
• **Spiracles' **external openings, which act as muscular valves in some insects, lead to the internal respiratory system, a densely networked array of tubes known as tracheae.
 
• **Air entered through the spiracles into the tracheal tubes and diffuses into the body tissues**.​__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ​**Gills **are a **type of respiratory organ found in many aquatic animals**, including a number of worms, nearly all molluscs and crustaceans, some insect larvae, all fishes, and a few amphibians.
 
• The **diaphragm **is a thin, **dome-shaped muscle that sits below the lungs and heart muscle that helps to inhale and exhale (breathe in and out).**

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of Aves (birds) class of animals?

options.text: The skin is dry without glands except the oil gland at the base of the tail.
The hind limbs are modified into wings.
The presence of feathers and most of them can fly except flightless birds.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The hind limbs are modified into wings**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Forelimbs and hindlimbs **are found on birds. The forelimbs are transformed into wings.
 
• Scales cover the hindlimbs, which are specialised for walking, jumping, and grasping tree branches. Birds have a **warm-blooded nature**.
 
• **Aves** are a group of endothermic animals that include birds.
 
• These animals belong to the Chordata phylum and have characteristics such as toothless jaws with a beak, hard-shelled eggs, and so on.
 
• In the terrestrial animal realm, there are an estimated 9000 Aves species. This species' most prominent attribute is its ability to fly.
 
• Their skeletal structure, which is made up of strong but hollow bones, allows them to fly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The fact that they are bipedal feathered animals is one of the most noticeable traits of the Aves class.
 
• Birds' forelimbs have evolved into wings that allow them to fly.
 
• Their back limbs have evolved into legs that aid them in swimming, walking, and other activities. Birds' legs often have four toes.
 
• Two or three toes, on the other hand, are rarely noticeable.

questions.question: One of the ______, the giant redwood tree Sequoia is one of the tallest tree species.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**gymnosperms**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The giant tree belonging to the family of **Sequoia** sempervirens is known as Red Wood__.
 
• Sequoia sempervirens are the only living species of the genus Sequoia in the cypress family Cupressaceae.
 
• They are also referred to as redwood, coastal redwood, etc.
 
• It is the tallest, evergreen, and long-lived gymnosperm.
 
• The leaves of gymnosperms are well adapted to extremes of climate.
 
• The height of a plant has reached 377 ft tall with a trunk of 9 m in diameter.
 
• The Sequoia sempervirens are **gymnosperms** since they do not possess flowers.
 
• They are present mainly in the mountains where precipitation from the approaching dampness off the sea is more prominent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__** 

__
 
• Gymnosperm: 

 
 
• The term Gymnosperm comes from the Greek words gymnos meaning "naked" and sperma meaning "seed".
 
• Gymnosperms are non-flowering, seed-bearing plants.
 
• Fruits are not formed due to the lack of floral parts.
 
• Seeds are formed on the inner side of scale-like leaves that are spirally arranged into a cone.
 
 

Explanation:__

__
 
• The endosperm is the primary source of food for the developing embryo.
 
• In gymnosperms, the endosperm is formed before fertilization.
 
• It is formed from the female gametophytic cells and is haploid.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Mosses from tiny gametophytes are the dominant step of the life cycle. Green, flat structures resembling true leaves, but lacking in vascular tissue, are attached in a spiral to the central stem or seta.
 
• **Pteridophytes **don't produce flowers and seeds hence they reproduce using spores.
 
 
• Pteridophytes are also known as cryptogams.
 
• Ferns and Azolla are some examples of Pteridophytes.
 
 
 
• Liverworts are a group of non-vascular plants similar to mosses.
 
 
• They do not produce seeds, flowers, fruit or wood, and even lack vascular tissue.
 
• Instead of seeds, liverworts produce spores for reproduction.

questions.question: Crayfish and ticks are classified into ______, respectively.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Crustacean and Arachnida.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Crayfish are freshwater crustaceans.**
 
• **Ticks are parasitic arachnids that are part of the mite superorder Parasitiformes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Crustacean
 
 
 
• **Crustaceans are arthropods**. Their skeletons are on the outside of their bodies.
 
• Crustaceans** have jointed parts so they can move.** They often have many legs.
 
• **Shrimp, crabs, lobsters, barnacles and hermit crabs are all crustaceans**.
 
• Crustaceans have two pairs of antennae.
 
 
 
 

 Arachnida
 
 
 
• **Body segmentation - usually consisting of a head, thorax, and abdomen**. Jointed appendages.
 
• A firm but** flexible exoskeleton.**
 
• An** open circulatory system** - blood is free-flowing in the body, not contained in vessels.
 
• **Spiders, daddy longlegs, false scorpions, mites, and ticks.**
 
 
 
 

 Myriapoda
 
 
 
• The** Myriapoda is a subphylum of arthropods.** It contains the millipedes, centipedes, and others.
 
• **Myriapods have a single pair of antennae and, in most cases, simple eyes.**
 
• Myriapods** breathe through spiracles** that connect to a tracheal system similar to that of insects.
 
 
 
 

 Insecta
 
 
 
• **Insects have what we call an exoskeleton **or a hard, shell-like covering on the outside of their body.
 
• Insects have** three main body parts: head, thorax, and abdomen.**
 
• Insects have** three pairs of legs**. They use the legs for walking, but sometimes an insect may have a pair of legs that are specially designed for jumping. Insects have two pairs of wings.

questions.question: Which of the following animals has more than one heart?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Octopus.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

 
• Octopuses have three hearts, a systemic heart that circulates blood around the body and two branchial hearts that pump it through each of the two gills.
 
• The systemic heart is inactive when the animal is swimming and thus it tires quickly and prefers to crawl.
 
• Octopus blood contains the copper-rich protein hemocyanin to transport oxygen.
 
• This makes the blood very viscous and it requires considerable pressure to pump it around the body.
 
• Octopus's blood pressures can exceed 75 mmHg.
 
• All octopuses are venomous, evidence shows that the animal does not make the venom by itself, but are produced by symbiotic bacteria instead.
 
• The blue-ringed octopus is the most venomous to humans and they are fatal.
 
• These sea or marine creatures lack the skeletal system and are grouped into:
 
 
• Kingdom: Animalia 
 
• Phylum: Mollusca
 
• Class: Cephalopoda
 
• Genus: Octopus

questions.question: Which of the following is **NOT **a unicellular organism?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Plants**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• All living organisms are made up of one or more units called cells.
 
• Organisms consist of only one cell is called a unicellular organism.
 
• Amoeba is an example of a unicellular organism.
 
• Other examples of the unicellular organisms are:
 
 
• Chlamydomonas.
 
• Protozoa
 
• Paramoecium.
 
• **Bacteria.**
 
• Nostoc.
 
• Yeast.
 
 
 
• Many cells group together in a single body and assume different functions in it to form various body parts in multicellular organisms.
 
• Examples of a multicellular organism are:
 
 
• **Plants.**
 
• Animals.
 
• Fungi.
 
• Algae.
 
 
 
• **Hence Plants is the correct answer.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Every multi-cellular organism has come from a single cell.
 
• All cells come from pre-existing cells.
 
• If an organism has no cell, it is called acellular.
 
 
• Virus is an example of an acellular organism.
